record.title: Pelican-Sim pairs numeric robot actions with rendered motion cues and reports downstream gains in RoboTwin
record.summary: A September 10 technical report from the Beijing Innovation Center of Humanoid Robotics describes Pelican-Sim 1.0, an action-conditioned video world model that combines a 28-dimensional robot-configuration vector with camera-aligned, URDF-rendered arm-motion cues, sparse mixture-of-experts layers and a distilled four-step rollout model. The authors report improved video-prediction metrics over evaluated baselines on AgiBotWorld Beta, RoboMIND and RoboTwin. In RoboTwin randomized tests, augmenting 10, 30 or 50 demonstrations per task with ten generated trajectories per demonstration raised policy success from 28.5% to 64.5%, 57.0% to 87.0%, and 70.0% to 93.0%, respectively, over five tasks and 200 unseen seeds per task. A world-model-plus-VLM evaluator reportedly ranked five policy checkpoints with Pearson correlation 0.994 after 1,000 task-specific adaptation rollouts; the test replayed the same action trajectories in the world model and simulator. The results are author-reported and primarily simulation-bounded. They do not establish physical-robot policy improvement, independent replication, or reliable closed-loop deployment under model-generated observations.
organizations: Beijing Innovation Center of Humanoid Robotics

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Pelican-Sim 1.0 combines a 28-dimensional action-value representation with URDF- and camera-rendered whole-arm action videos in a sparse-MoE video diffusion model and reports a four-step causal rollout path.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: On three held-out robot-video datasets, the paper reports PSNR improvements over its strongest evaluated baselines of 4.636 dB on AgiBotWorld Beta, 2.080 dB on RoboMIND and 10.343 dB on RoboTwin.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: In RoboTwin randomized evaluation, adding 100, 300 or 500 generated rollouts per task to 10, 30 or 50 original demonstrations is associated with reported policy success changes of 28.5%→64.5%, 57.0%→87.0% and 70.0%→93.0%, respectively, across five tasks and 200 unseen seeds per task.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: A world-model-plus-VLM estimator reportedly reaches Pearson r=0.994 and perfect rank correlation across five policy checkpoints after 1,000 task-specific adaptation rollouts, using matched action trajectories on 200 held-out conditions per checkpoint; the protocol does not test closed-loop policy execution under generated observations.

claims.label: INFERRED
claims.text: The paper's downstream policy gains and ranking measurements do not establish corresponding gains on physical robots, independent replication, or transfer beyond the reported task and simulator regime.

evidence_gaps.description: The reported video, policy-augmentation and policy-ranking measurements have not been independently reproduced; code/checkpoint availability and immutable artifact identity were not checked in this activation.

The downstream utility claims are concentrated in RoboTwin and do not establish policy gains on physical robots or under closed-loop execution from generated observations. The ranking experiment replays fixed action trajectories.

The world model's downstream pipeline relies on a fine-tuned Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct evaluator for success estimates, candidate ranking and rewards; the reported effects may depend on evaluator calibration and validity filtering.

brief.importance_rationale: If these bounded results hold, one action-conditioned world-model pipeline can improve the efficiency of simulated robot data generation and provide usable policy ranking signals, potentially changing how robotics teams allocate costly physical trials. The result is notable rather than field-shifting because the downstream evidence is author-reported, concentrated in RoboTwin, uses only five tasks for policy studies, and has no independent or physical-robot outcome validation in this review.
limitations: All headline metrics in this record are reported by the paper authors; the research desk did not run the model or independently reproduce them.
The strongest synthetic-data policy outcomes are evaluated in RoboTwin randomized simulation, not on physical robot tasks.
The policy-ranking experiment replays the same policy action trajectories in the world model and simulator; it does not test closed-loop policy execution under generated observations.

Policy ranking uses only five checkpoints from a training run and 200 held-out initial conditions per checkpoint; the reported Pearson correlation does not establish broader calibration or deployment reliability.
The action-selection and policy-improvement pipelines depend on a fine-tuned Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct evaluator, so world-model and evaluator errors can affect the apparent utility.
The generation-time comparison excludes training and upstream preparation, so it does not establish full lifecycle economics or net dollar savings.
The reviewed v1 report describes code and checkpoint release as future work; no immutable artifact or independent reproduction was inspected.

brief.summary: A September 10 technical report from the Beijing Innovation Center of Humanoid Robotics describes Pelican-Sim 1.0, an action-conditioned video world model that combines a 28-dimensional robot-configuration vector with camera-aligned, URDF-rendered arm-motion cues, sparse mixture-of-experts layers and a distilled four-step rollout model. A world-model-plus-VLM evaluator reportedly ranked five policy checkpoints with Pearson correlation 0.994 after 1,000 task-specific adaptation rollouts; the test replayed the same action trajectories in the world model and simulator. The results are author-reported and primarily simulation-bounded. They do not establish physical-robot policy improvement, independent replication, or reliable closed-loop deployment under model-generated observations.

technical.claimed_result: The authors report that joint numeric and rendered-motion conditioning, mixed-domain training and sparse experts improve action-conditioned video metrics, and that the resulting simulator supports data augmentation, action selection, policy ranking and simulated policy improvement.
technical.compute_or_cost: The report measures generation throughput at 24 seconds per trajectory on a GPU versus 60 seconds for manual robot collection, and 19 seconds versus 55 seconds for RoboTwin simulation. These are author-reported generation timings; they exclude upstream training, simulator/model construction and initial-frame preparation, and do not establish total lifecycle cost or dollar savings.
technical.demonstrated_result: The inspected arXiv v1 paper reports held-out benchmark and downstream RoboTwin measurements. No run of its code or model was performed in this activation, so numerical outcomes remain CLAIMED rather than independently demonstrated by the research desk.
technical.implementation_status: The report describes an academic technical system and links a public project and code repository. Its v1 text says checkpoints and inference code will be released; artifact availability and reproducibility were not checked or run in this activation.
technical.mechanism: A video diffusion transformer predicts future RGB observations from an initial frame, task instruction and frame-aligned robot configuration sequence. A unified 28-dimensional action-value pathway carries numerical joint/gripper/hand state; a synchronized action-video pathway renders whole-arm joint positions and links from robot URDF and camera calibration. The model interleaves both conditions and uses sparse shared and routed experts. Causal adaptation and few-step distillation reduce the reported 21-frame rollout from 35 denoising steps to four.
technical.novelty: The engineering contribution is a synchronized action interface that retains numerical robot configuration while making whole-arm motion explicit in camera space, combined with sparse experts and a fast causal rollout path. The paper evaluates downstream use of the predictor rather than only visual fidelity.
technical.regime: The report trains on approximately one million real and simulated trajectories and evaluates video prediction on held-out AgiBotWorld Beta, RoboMIND and RoboTwin splits. Downstream policy augmentation, action selection, policy evaluation and policy improvement are principally tested in RoboTwin's randomized configuration across five tasks. Augmentation evaluations use 200 unseen seeds per task. Policy ranking applies identical action trajectories to simulator and world model on 200 held-out initial conditions for each of five checkpoints.
technical.reproducibility: The report provides detailed protocols and links code, but this review did not inspect a pinned code revision, model checkpoint, raw evaluation traces or independent reproduction. Results are one author team's measurements.
technical.strongest_baseline: For video metrics, the paper compares against the strongest available evaluated world-model baseline per dataset, including Ctrl-World. The data-generation comparison uses randomized RoboTwin trajectories and policies trained with identical configurations. The action-selection comparison includes single-sample, random-of-10, VLM-direct and Ctrl-World selection under matched candidate pools and a shared VLM evaluator.

brief.title: Pelican-Sim pairs numeric robot actions with rendered motion cues and reports downstream gains in RoboTwin
brief.why_it_matters: If the reported effects persist beyond RoboTwin, an action-conditioned video simulator could make robot data collection and early policy evaluation cheaper by using generated trajectories and predicted outcomes before executing every candidate physically. This paper is notable because it evaluates one model across data augmentation, action selection, policy evaluation and simulated policy improvement, while exposing the added dependency on a separately fine-tuned VLM evaluator. The paper does not yet show that the reported gains transfer to physical robot outcomes or remain reliable when policies act on generated observations.
